findings.document_finding: The 1951 experimental Easter Vigil, 16 November 1955 decree, compulsory 25 March 1956 start, and restoration of evening/night services are stated by the decree.
findings.qualification: Supports corrected chronology; not an evaluation of every Holy Week rubrical change.

findings.locator: SSPX, 'Religious liberty in the declaration Dignitatis humanae', §§2, critique of State indifference
findings.document_finding: The Society argues that an external civil right to false religious practice presupposes State neutrality to religious truth; it explicitly distinguishes individual from civil indifferentism.
findings.qualification: Supports attributed SSPX objection; not proof that it is doctrinally correct.

findings.locator: Canon 144, §§1–2, in Code of Canon Law Book I, Title VIII
findings.document_finding: Supplied executive power arises in common error or positive and probable doubt; applies also to specifically enumerated faculties.
findings.qualification: Does not itself support unlimited permanent emergency jurisdiction.

findings.document_finding: Six named bishops' incurred latae sententiae penalties are declared in connection with recent episcopal consecrations.
findings.qualification: Do not conflate this 2026 event with the five bishops mentioned in the 1988 document.

findings.document_finding: The DDF declares SSPX clerical status and laity's formal adherence distinctions, plus illicit ministry and invalid confession/marriage assistance.
findings.qualification: Official published DDF position, not independent verification of each individual sacramental act.

findings.document_finding: Society claims filing preliminary recourse on 11 July and suspensive execution under canon 1353.
findings.qualification: Proven Society's claim; no final recourse ruling in the checked records.

findings.locator: Canon 1353, Book VI, Title V on application of penalties
findings.document_finding: Appeal or recourse against a court judgment or decree imposing/declaring a penalty has suspensive effect.
findings.qualification: This canon is about penal execution and does not grant faculties for marriage/confession.

findings.document_finding: Preliminary petition, administrative recourse, varied effects on execution, and salvation-of-souls principle are separately regulated.
findings.qualification: Do not confuse automatic suspension of penal act with general administrative recourse rules.

findings.document_finding: John Paul II describes episcopal consecrations of 30 June, calls act schismatic, states named men incurred excommunication.
findings.qualification: Original draft's 'imposed penalties' was corrected to 'stated incurred'.

findings.locator: Prologue and linked theological/canonical 1999 SiSiNoNo study
findings.document_finding: Original SSPX-hosted 1999 study expressly defends an extraordinary state of necessity and acknowledges absence of pontifical mandate.
findings.qualification: It is a later 1999 apologia, not a 1988 General House document.

findings.locator: Humanae vitae (1968), §§11–14 on marriage and contraception
findings.document_finding: Paul VI links each marital act to procreation and prohibits directly contraceptive methods.
findings.qualification: Source directly supports rule; sociological predictions not established by these passages alone.

findings.locator: Charles E. Curran byline 16 October 1986, opening paragraphs
findings.document_finding: Curran himself defends theological dissent on certain non-infallible teachings, while acknowledging special hierarchical teaching office and duty of religious respect.
findings.qualification: First-person proponent material, distinct from CDF description; later article is not verbatim 1983–86 exchange.

findings.locator: CDF letter to Curran 25 July 1986, opening and substantive response
findings.document_finding: CDF quotes Curran's own response and rejects his proposed restricted teaching appointment.
findings.qualification: Institutional party's response, not sole source for Curran's complete arguments.

findings.document_finding: Instruction recognises difficulties in non-definitive interventions, including some contingent elements; also recommends responsible dialogue and opposes parallel magisterium.
findings.qualification: Must not be misrepresented as forbidding all serious questioning.

findings.document_finding: Three categories of assent: revealed, definitive non-revealed, and authentic non-definitive.
findings.qualification: Supports draft classification, not global certification of every example.

findings.document_finding: The encyclical sets out a description of proportionalism/consequentialism and rejects exceptions to moral absolutes.
findings.qualification: This is a critic's presentation; original proponents' own texts remain to be compared before independently certifying opponent-attribution.

findings.locator: Promulgated document, not archived preparatory schemas
findings.document_finding: The promulgated constitution establishes authoritative final teaching.
findings.qualification: Does not by itself verify reasons specific preparatory schemas were rejected; historical archive remains missing.

outstanding: Exact original 1962 preconciliar schemas for CR-ORG-07 were not inspected, so motivations for each rejected draft remain uncertified.
CR-MOR-05 cites Veritatis splendor as a critical Roman description of proportionalism; a direct original opposing theologian passage is still required to certify the position.
No expert canonical adjudication of the effect of 2026 SSPX recourse is evidenced; canon 1353 concerns penal execution, while particular faculties require separate assessment.
French revisions are substantive drafts checked for bilingual equivalence only, not native-language publication approval.
These findings are a bounded first editorial pass and do not flip original_context_approved, theological_approval, or publication_allowed for any canonical owner.
